neutral_facts.value: The accused persons, who were armed with weapons, approached the victim and another individual near a cycle stand at a college campus. They demanded that the victim and the other individual withdraw their names from a college election. When they refused, the accused assaulted them. The victim sustained severe injuries and later succumbed to his injuries. The other individual also received injuries and lodged a complaint with the police. The prosecution presented eyewitness accounts, medical reports, and statements from witnesses to establish that the victim died as a result of the assault. The accused were present at the scene and participated in the attack, with specific roles in causing injuries to the victim. The investigation had some flaws, such as the non-recovery of weapons and delayed recovery of a blood-stained shirt, but the medical evidence and testimonies of the prosecution witnesses supported the prosecution's case. The accused were found to have formed an unlawful assembly with the common object of preventing the victim from contesting the election, and the circumstances indicated that a common intention to kill may have arisen on the spur of the moment.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the accused persons, armed with weapons, asked the victim and PW 1 to withdraw their names from the college election. On refusal, they assaulted the victim, leading to his death. The medical evidence and testimonies of the prosecution witnesses corroborated that the deceased died a homicidal death. The presence and participation of all accused in the offence were established, and the common intention to kill might have arisen on the spur of the moment.

quotes.text: Medical evidence corroborated by testimonies of the prosecution witnesses proved that the deceased died a homicidal death.
The presence and participation of all the accused in the offence were established, and the common intention to kill might have arisen on the spur of the moment.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that there was an improvement by the prosecution witnesses with respect to the place of occurrence of the incident. They also questioned the credibility of the prosecution witnesses, the medical evidence, and the absence of a common object of killing. The counsel for the appellants submitted that the prosecution story was unbelievable and that the deceased could have died due to falling on the ground.

quotes.text: The appellants raised the defense that there was an improvement by the prosecution witnesses with respect to the place of occurrence of the incident.
The prosecution story is unbelievable as, according to the prosecution, the incident took place at two places.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the common object of an unlawful assembly may form on the spur of the moment, and the common intention to kill might have arisen at that time. The Court also emphasized that the testimony of an injured eye witness should be given much credence when supported by medical evidence.

quotes.text: The common object of an unlawful assembly may form on the spur of the moment, and the common intention to kill might have arisen at that time.
The testimony of an injured eye witness has to be given much credence when supported by medical evidence.
